study: Jay et al. 2017 — EEF Dialogic Teaching (Sheffield Hallam evaluation)
eval_evidence: EEF-commissioned efficacy trial independently evaluated by Sheffield Hallam University; the developer team (CPRT/York) separately ran its own video analysis but the impact evaluation was the independent evaluator's.
developer_evidence: Report: the intervention was 'developed and delivered by a team from the Cambridge Primary Review Trust (CPRT) and the University of York,' with training 'led by Robin Alexander' (the developer). The developer team delivered the training and ongoing support.
cascade_evidence: The developer/delivery team trained the Year 5 class teachers (and a nominated school mentor + headteacher) directly via induction and plenary sessions; the school mentor is an in-school support/peer role for that school's teachers, not a developer-replacing cascade trainer.
counterfactual_evidence: Cluster RCT with control schools continuing 'business as usual'; no alternative PD assigned to controls.
coaching_evidence: Programme included 'ongoing in-school monitoring and support': each school appointed a mentor supporting Year 5 teachers across eleven plan/review/refocus cycles, with recurring mentoring sessions and video/audio self-evaluation of the teacher's own lessons — recurring in-class support cycles.
student_dose_evidence: Dialogic Teaching is a pedagogical approach delivered by the regular Year 5 class teacher within normal across-curriculum lessons; no tutoring, pull-out, extra minutes, or student-facing software added.
maturity_evidence: Two-term intervention measured at immediate post-test (May 2016) in its first/only implementation year; teachers were new to the approach.
